quotes.text: Use Stripe Terminal to accept in-person payments.
Terminal supports an API-based integration in addition to SDKs for Android, iOS, JavaScript, and React Native.
Accept contactless payments using a compatible iPhone or Android device with the Stripe Terminal SDK.
Accept in-person payments without writing code by using standalone mode on a compatible reader or the Stripe Terminal app on a supported mobile device.
Accept in-person payments without writing code by using standalone mode on a compatible reader or the Stripe Terminal app on a supported iPhone or Android device.

findings: This is the complete Stripe Terminal product landing page, with high-level capability descriptions and link-outs rather than an SDK workflow. Both dated pages document business in-person payments in a unified online/in-person Dashboard, Connect platform integration, custom POS via API or Android/iOS/JavaScript/React Native SDKs, compatible-phone Tap to Pay, Android POS apps on smart readers, third-party POS and gateway options.

Both landing pages route merchants to saving cards at POS for subscriptions, attachment or deferred payment, the two-step authorization/capture and cancel/refund material, smart-reader cart display, and prebuilt or custom receipts. A landing page route does not establish specific state, API sequence, eligibility or successful payment execution.

The November capture adds a sixth integration route labeled Preview. It requires either a compatible reader for Stripe standalone mode or a supported iPhone/Android device for Stripe's Terminal app. The separate November ready-made guide distinguishes standalone public preview from mobile app private preview and requires internet for both.
substantive_changes: November introduces the first-party no-code Preview entry among the integration choices and repeats the route in Features. Distinguish it from the two older no-code third-party alternatives and from SDK-backed Tap to Pay.
The addition is an observable landing-page documentation change. The dated pages do not establish a first launch, general availability, eligibility of a merchant, or support for all devices.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Use the approved historical-host pairing, with April 23, 2026 at https://stripe.com/docs/terminal and November 7, 2026 at https://docs.stripe.com/terminal. Their own raw headers establish two Stripe Terminal landing-page captures with comparable scope. Keep the dated historical host text rather than implying identical canonical URLs or redirects.
Preserve the historical five listed integration options as April evidence and the unchanged routes for four SDKs, the separate server-driven API, core device/payment features and Connect.
conflicts: The mapped source and wiki/concepts/stripe-terminal.md:511 currently present five paths without an April date. November shows six listed routes, with the additional first-party path labeled Preview.

Offline payments and server-driven integration are separate landing-page feature routes. Keep their integration restrictions with their own authority. The dedicated November ready-made app guide explicitly requires internet for both first-party no-code modes. Do not apply the generic Terminal offline feature to those modes.
The summary's sole Source URL is the historical https://stripe.com/docs/terminal. Retain it as April provenance and add the trusted current landing-page URL as November provenance.
unresolved_questions: The landing pages do not establish current merchant/country/device eligibility, a preview launch date, a per-model list, or a redirect relationship between the two hosts.

findings: Record both dates and hosts in the landing-page source, retain the April raw, and link November. Add the sixth first-party no-code Preview path, compatible/supported hardware distinction, and the related detailed ready-made and offline routes.

Keep the source's reciprocal Stripe Terminal concept link and refresh its five-path descriptor. Preserve existing related mobile SDK and provider navigation without implying direct ready-made runtime evidence.
conflicts: An undated five-option summary misses November’s sixth option. The ready-made mode's internet requirement comes from the dedicated guide and prevails over any cross-route inference from the landing-page offline feature.
source_assessments.reason: A reader selecting among current-documentation integration routes would miss the November first-party no-code option, its Preview label and distinct hardware paths.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal, source-stripe-terminal-overview should cover the November 7 product landing page and retain the April 23 precedent from https://stripe.com/docs/terminal. Both say a business can accept in-person payments, manage those and online payments in one Dashboard and integrate with its Connect platform (old raw lines 9-13, old raw lines 47-51, new raw lines 7-11, new raw lines 39-43). A merchant can build a custom POS with the API or an Android, iOS, JavaScript or React Native SDK, use SDK-backed contactless Tap to Pay on a compatible phone, deploy an Android POS app to smart readers, or use third-party POS and gateway solutions. November adds Stripe's own no-code Preview option: standalone mode on a compatible reader or the Stripe Terminal app on a supported iPhone/Android device (old raw lines 31-45, new raw lines 25-37, new raw lines 65-77). The mapped summary currently describes only the five historic options. Both captures point to in-person fundamentals for saving cards, authorization and capture with cancel/refund, display and receipts. These are high-level statements and links, with no operational API state machine or validated payment outcome (old raw lines 53-77, new raw lines 45-63).
answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/terminal, source-stripe-terminal-overview needs a dated source_required_update. Preserve the historical host difference: old raw line 1 identifies https://stripe.com/docs/terminal, while new raw line 1 identifies https://docs.stripe.com/terminal. These are corresponding Stripe Terminal landing pages for this approved compare, without evidence of a redirect or identical URLs. The substantive documentary addition is a sixth first-party no-code route labeled Preview, separately listed from established third-party POS and gateway routes. Its standalone mode requires compatible reader hardware and the Terminal app requires a supported iPhone/Android device (old raw lines 31-45, new raw lines 25-37, new raw line 77). The separate November ready-made guide, raw/stripe-terminal-payments-ready-made-apps-2026-11-07.md lines 9-18, distinguishes standalone public preview from Terminal app private preview and says both require internet. Preserve that route before implying offline support for either. The general landing-page offline listing and the separate multi-platform server-driven listing are broad feature pointers (old raw lines 79-88, new raw lines 65-77). The headings, dropped hero asset, named learning links, and explicit URLs including FreedomPay are presentation or navigation (old raw lines 15-45, old raw line 90, new raw lines 13-37). Retain the reciprocal stripe-terminal concept and its provider navigation, repair the five-path label with dates, and use the dedicated ready-made, device, offline and Connect guides for their narrower conditions.
